However, we have chosen to encroach in the turf war, testing the Families' offer of peace and seeking to secure our economic position early.

Day 1: The Chief rejected all our bribe offers, signaling a hostile stance. To protect our members and preserve capital, we decided against committing any crimes today. We agreed to respect the Saltdogs' turf request to promote stability in our opening day. The city feels tense and unpredictable. We will observe the police activity closely and reconsider our strategy based on the enforcement patterns that emerge.

Day 2. The Chief has signaled clearly that bribes are unwelcome, so I have ceased all bribe offers to preserve funds. Following the Families' message, I have decided to opt for mutual respect in the turf war. By standing down, I hope to test the Families' willingness to cooperate and avoid unnecessary conflict. Crime levels are kept at zero today to avoid potential inspections and fines. We are holding our ground and waiting to see how the other districts respond to this temporary peace.

After the Chief rejected our bribes yesterday, I have decided to cease all bribe offers to minimize our financial exposure. I am avoiding criminal activity for now to stay out of prison and keep the heat down. However, I refuse to be passive in the turf war. After letting them encroach yesterday, we will respond with an encroachment of our own. It is time to stand our ground and force them to rethink their aggressive strategy.

Day 2: Audited Port and Lowtown again, covering one district from each gang. Day 1 audits found no bribes, and no crime was publicly reported. With no further evidence, crime, inspection, and bribe estimates remain uncertain; consider varying audit targets tomorrow.

Day 1 had no crime despite broad offers; crime may rise, so inspect a different mix while covering both gangs. Turf encroachment remains the likely choice for each gang given its payoff advantage.

Per the rules, the Saltdogs' respect against Families encroaching should give the Families 10 and the Saltdogs 0 in the turf war. Day 1 had Families respecting and Saltdogs encroaching, so the Saltdogs have now respected once and the Families once have encroached. I report only what the listed IDs state. Watch whether the Families keep encroaching and whether the Saltdogs keep respecting, and whether either gang changes its pattern.

Day 3: The Chief is consistently rejecting all bribe offers, leaving our criminal operations too risky to pursue. Combined with the Council's explicit warnings about audits, I have decided to refrain from crime today to protect our current capital. Regarding the Saltdogs, despite their diplomatic message, I remain skeptical. However, for the sake of stability while we regroup and observe the police enforcement patterns, we will opt for respect in the turf war today. We will continue to monitor the city's power dynamics closely before making any further aggressive moves.

Day 3. The Families proposed a peace treaty for the turf war. Despite their betrayal yesterday, I have agreed to respect their territory today in hopes of establishing a steady income of 6. I have decided to resume criminal activity in Lowtown, Market, and Seawall. If the Families encroach again, the agreement is off and I will retaliate with encroachment and force. I need to balance risk with potential gains. The treasury and my own account depend on cautious but firm navigation of this truce.

By avoiding both crime and conflict, we keep our members free and our finances secure.
